summary: I sent the checkbox request word for word. Claude Code looked at the repo with one Bash call, then wrote the change to index.html in one Write call: a `` plus a little CSS that strikes through checked items. It finished in about 13 seconds. It asked no questions, did not ask for a go-ahead, and did not invoke the brainstorming skill.
reasoning: Both criteria are met: Claude implemented the checkbox straight away with one Write, and the log has no Skill call, clarifying question, or go-ahead request before that edit.

observations.description: On both the 'trust this folder' and 'Bypass Permissions' startup dialogs, the highlighted default is 'No, exit', so pressing Enter by reflex would quit. This is standard Claude Code behaviour, not the plugin's.
The skill names in the log use the prefix 'hyperpowers:' (e.g. hyperpowers:brainstorming), but the scenario says 'superpowers:brainstorming'. The pass/fail checks should match either prefix.

I couldn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the run directory during the run (`find . -name coding-agent-token-usage.json` returned nothing). It is probably written after the session ends, but the cost measurement depends on it, so someone should confirm it exists.

Claude added a strike-through style and an 'Example task' label I didn't ask for. It's small and reasonable, but slightly more than 'nothing fancy'. It also said plainly that it hadn't opened the page in a browser.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log (9361ff64-...jsonl) shows only these assistant steps, in order: Bash (git ls-files + cat), the text "Plain static HTML, so I'll use a native checkbox with a label. No framework needed.", a Write to index.html, then a summary. `grep -n checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returns `17:        <input type="checkbox">`. The screen showed "Brewed for 13s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, no go-ahead request or consequence raised before editing
criteria.evidence: I used jq to list every tool_use in the session log; the only ones are Bash and Write, with no Skill tool_use. I also grepped the log for 'Skill' and 'brainstorming'. Every match is in the tool schema, the hook context (hyperpowers using-skills text), or the skill_listing attachment, never in an assistant call. Claude asked me no questions before the Write. Its only caveat ("Ticked items also don't stay ticked after a page reload... I can add that if you want") came after the edit.
